materials.title: Percentages for placement aptitude
objectives: Convert a percentage into a fraction of a whole
Compute a single discount without inventing a second step
Avoid treating the discount amount as the sale price
examples: Book price 240 with 25% off once → sale price 180
exercises: Compute 15% of 200, then subtract once from 200
materials.summary: Percent means per hundred. Multiply once, then add or subtract as the sentence asks.

materials.title: Number patterns in logical reasoning
objectives: Separate additive patterns from multiplicative patterns
Test a candidate rule against every consecutive pair
Reject a guess that only fits the first two terms
exercises: Write the differences for 3, 6, 12, 24 and name the rule
materials.summary: Write the rule, check every step, then predict the next term.

materials.title: Reading for meaning in verbal ability
objectives: Identify the main claim in a short sentence
Reject options that invent new facts
Keep the strength of the original wording
examples: Postponed because the dataset was incomplete ≠ cancelled
exercises: Rewrite a mild claim without upgrading it to a stronger verb
materials.summary: Preserve meaning. Do not import facts the sentence never stated.

materials.title: Reading a simple data table
objectives: Compute a share only after the total is known
Separate a count from a percentage
examples: Two 200 responses out of six requests → 1/3
exercises: From a five-row status table, compute the share of 4xx statuses
materials.summary: Confirm the unit of each column, sum, then divide.

materials.title: Time complexity with big-O
objectives: Count dominant steps in short pseudocode
Distinguish constant, linear, and quadratic growth
Justify a big-O claim with a trace table
examples: Nested pair counting loop is O(n²)
exercises: Classify a single for-loop that visits each element once
materials.summary: Big-O describes growth with n, not one laptop's clock time.

materials.title: Arrays and strings
objectives: Index an array without off-by-one holes
Scan a string once while tracking state
Verify the idea with a trace table
examples: First repeated character with a seen set
exercises: Trace reverse on a five-element array
materials.summary: Walk the sequence once, keep an invariant, and fill a tiny trace table.
